title: Void Ending in a Trine to Sun
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Sun, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his light and his generative heat. Picatrix calls the Sun the light of the world and the axis on which the universe turns; generative power flows from him, the heart is his seat in the body, gold is his metal, and the ruby and the jacinth his stones. His benevolence fits great royal achievements and kings. The whole lunar doctrine hangs on him, for in the text's accounting the stars and the Moon together sustain all vegetation and every composite body.
